refs.note: Usage guide for RisuAI trigger scripts (Lua mode)
refs.text:
RisuAI - Trigger Script (Lua Mode): Usage Guide
Source: https://kwaroran.github.io/docs/srp/lua

OVERVIEW
In Lua mode, a trigger script lets you write a Lua script that runs when a
trigger event occurs. The script is executed from the beginning every time
an event fires, so any data you want to keep between runs must be stored in
chat variables or state variables.

1. CALLBACK FUNCTIONS

───

Standard callbacks you can define in your script:

onStart(triggerId) Called when a chat message is sent.
onOutput(triggerId) Called when the AI response is received.
onInput(triggerId) Called when user input is received.

Button events:
For buttons such as {{button::Display::TriggerName}}, the function whose
name matches TriggerName is called (e.g. TriggerName(triggerId)).

Edit listeners:
listenEdit(type, callback)
• type: "editRequest", "editDisplay", "editInput", or "editOutput"
• callback signature: callback(triggerId, data)
• The callback returns the modified data.

Examples:

-- Alert when user input is received
function onInput(triggerId)
alertNormal(triggerId, "input received!")
end

-- Prepend a prefix (stored in state) to the displayed message
listenEdit("editDisplay", function(triggerId, data)
local prefix = getState(triggerId, "prefix") or ""
return prefix .. data
end)

-- Handle a button: {{button::Display::onButton}}
function onButton(triggerId)
alertNormal(triggerId, "button clicked!")
end

2. AVAILABLE FUNCTIONS

───

General rules:
• Every function except log() must receive triggerId as its first
argument (for security). Get it from the callback function.
• In the editDisplay event, only these work: setChatVar, getChatVar,
setState, getState, log. All others do not.
• Functions marked [LOW LEVEL ACCESS] require low-level access permission.
• Functions marked [ASYNC] must be awaited with :await(), e.g.
similarity(triggerId, source, value):await()

Logging
log(message)
Logs to the console in JSON format (unlike print), so arrays and
objects display correctly in devtools.

Variables
setChatVar(triggerId, key, value)
Set a chat variable. value must be a string.
getChatVar(triggerId, key)
Get a chat variable's value.
setState(triggerId, key, value)
Set a state variable. value must be JSON-serializable (string, number,
boolean, array, object).
getState(triggerId, key)
Get a state variable's value.

Chat control
stopChat(triggerId)
Stop the chat. Only works in some trigger events.

Alerts
alertError(triggerId, message)
Show an error alert.
alertNormal(triggerId, message)
Show a normal alert.
alertInput(triggerId, message)
Show an input alert and return the value the user typed.

Chat messages (indexes are 0-based; role is "user" or "char")
setChat(triggerId, index, message)
Set the message at the given index.
setChatRole(triggerId, index, role)
Set the role of the message at the given index.
addChat(triggerId, role, message)
Append a message with the given role.
insertChat(triggerId, index, role, message)
Insert a message at the given index with the given role.
removeChat(triggerId, index)
Remove the message at the given index.
cutChat(triggerId, start, end)
Cut messages from start to end (both 0-based). To remove only one
message, use removeChat.
getChatLength(triggerId)
Get the number of chat messages.
getFullChat(triggerId)
Get the entire chat as a table:
{
{role = "user", data = "user message"},
{role = "char", data = "char message"},
...
}
setFullChat(triggerId, chat)
Replace the entire chat, using the same table format as getFullChat.

Character data
getName(triggerId) / setName(triggerId, name)
Get / set the current character's name.
getDescription(triggerId) / setDescription(triggerId, description)
Get / set the current character's description.
getCharacterFirstMessage(triggerId) / setCharacterFirstMessage(triggerId, message)
Get / set the current character's first message.
getBackgroundEmbedding(triggerId) / setBackgroundEmbedding(triggerId, embedding)
Get / set the current character's background embedding.

Advanced functions (all [LOW LEVEL ACCESS] and [ASYNC])
similarity(triggerId, source, value)
Sorts by similarity. source must be an array of strings; value must
be a string. Returns an array of indexes sorted by similarity.

generateImage(triggerId, prompt, negative)
Generates an image from the prompt and negative prompt. Returns the
asset CBS, e.g. {{asset::assetId}}.

LLM(triggerId, data)
Performs an LLM request. data is a message table; roles can be
"system", "assistant", or "user":
{
{role = "system", data = "system message"},
{role = "assistant", data = "char message"},
{role = "user", data = "user message"}
}
Returns:
{
success = true,
message = "response message",
}
simpleLLM(triggerId, message)
Performs a simple LLM request. Both the input and the returned
response are plain strings.

3. TIPS AND LIMITATIONS

───

• New to Lua? See the Lua 5.4 manual (https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/)
or ask an AI chatbot such as the RisuAI chat playground.
• The in-app editor is small; consider writing the script in an
external editor like VSCode, then pasting it into the app.
• Prefer log() over alert or print for debugging: it does not disturb
other functions and displays data more readably.
• Prefer setState/getState over setChatVar/getChatVar for storing data,
since they support more data types.
• The script re-runs from the beginning on every trigger, so persist
data with chat variables or state variables.
• json.lua (https://github.com/rxi/json.lua) is built in. Use
json.encode and json.decode to serialize/deserialize JSON.
• The script runs in a sandbox: no file system or network access.
• No external libraries other than the included json.lua.
• If an error occurs, the app behaves as if the script did not run, and
the error message is shown in the console.
• The Lua version is based on Lua 5.4.

refs.name: V2 트리거 참고 자료
refs.note: Reference for RisuAI trigger script V2
refs.text:
RisuAI - Trigger Script V2: Reference Guide

SOURCES AND CAVEAT
The official docs page (https://kwaroran.github.io/docs/srp/trigger/) is
currently only a stub: it contains a single sentence ("Trigger scripts are
scripts that run their effect when a specific event occurs and conditions
are met") and no V2 details.

The information below was therefore compiled from DeepWiki, an unofficial,
auto-generated wiki based on the RisuAI source code (src/ts/process/
triggers.ts and related files):
• https://deepwiki.com/kwaroran/RisuAI/5.2.2-trigger-script-system
• https://deepwiki.com/kwaroran/RisuAI/8.3-trigger-effects-reference
These pages describe a specific code snapshot, so details may differ in
newer RisuAI versions. The pages also say V2 has "90+" effect types but
list only a subset; this file includes only the effects actually named in
those pages, not a complete list.

1. WHAT IS A TRIGGER?

───

A trigger has four components:
type When the trigger executes (6 execution modes).
conditions Whether the trigger should run (var, exists, chatindex).
effect Actions to perform (90+ V2 effect types, 15 V1 types, or
embedded code).
lowLevelAccess Optional flag enabling privileged operations.
Low-level access must also be enabled in the character settings.

2. EXECUTION MODES

───

start Chat/character loaded. Initialize variables, set up state.
Full access.
manual Triggered by a user button or command (or called by name).
Full access.
input Before the AI request, when the user sends a message. Modify
user input, inject context. Full access.
output After the AI response. Process output, extract data. Full
access.
display While rendering chat messages. Dynamic UI content / state
display. RESTRICTED allow list.
request During prompt construction. Low-level prompt manipulation.
RESTRICTED allow list.

Display mode (read-only safe effects only; prevents rendering from
modifying persistent state):
• v2GetDisplayState, v2SetDisplayState (temporary, display-only state)
• all "safe subset" effects (string operations, calculations,
conditionals, read-only data access)

Request mode:
• v2GetRequestState, v2SetRequestState, v2GetRequestStateRole,
v2SetRequestStateRole, v2GetRequestStateLength
• all "safe subset" effects

Modules: triggers from enabled modules are automatically included, so
modules/plugins can inject logic globally or per character.

3. CONDITIONS

───

var Compare a variable or value against another value using
operators: =, !=, >, <, >=, <=, null, true.
exists Search recent messages for text using strict, loose, or regex
matching, with a configurable depth.
chatindex Compare the current chat message count against a number.

4. V1 vs V2 EFFECTS

───

V1 effects (legacy, kept for backward compatibility, not recommended for
new scripts):
setvar, cutchat, modifychat, systemprompt, impersonate, command, stop,
runtrigger, sendAIprompt, runImgGen, checkSimilarity, runLLM,
extractRegex, showAlert

V2 effects (current standard). Features:
• Indentation-based scoping for control flow structures
• Type-safe value handling with var/value type specification
• Local variables via v2DeclareLocalVar
• Enhanced control flow: if/else, loops, advanced conditions such as
approximate equality and "contains"
• Arrays and dictionaries
All V2 effect names start with the "v2" prefix (e.g. v2SetVar, v2If).

Code-based effects (embed code directly in a trigger):
triggercode JavaScript, with access to the trigger context
triggerlua Lua (via the wasmoon engine, run through runScripted)
py Python via a web worker using Pyodide
(See the separate Lua mode guide for the Lua API.)

5. VALUE TYPES: "value" vs "var"

───

Most V2 effects take valueType / sourceType / targetType parameters that
say whether a parameter is a literal or a variable reference:
value Literal value, parsed through CBS.
e.g. "Hello World" or "{{char}}"
var Variable name; the variable's value is retrieved.
e.g. if myVar contains "5", the result is "5"

6. VARIABLE SYSTEM AND SCOPING

───

Variables are looked up through a four-tier hierarchy (getVar), including
V2 local variables. Chat variables are stored in chat.scriptstate as a
key-value object with keys prefixed by "$", and persist within the chat.

Local variables (V2):
• Declared with v2DeclareLocalVar; they exist only within the control
structure (indent level) where they are declared.
• Each effect has an "indent" property that sets its scope level.
• Lookup goes from the current indent downward to indent 0.
• v2EndIndent clears all local variables at indents greater than or
equal to the ending indent.

7. V2 EFFECTS BY CATEGORY

───

Only effects named in the source pages are listed.

7.1 Special
v2Header code?: string, indent
Marks the start of a V2 trigger block.
v2Comment value: string, indent
Documentation comment.
v2DeclareLocalVar var, value, valueType ('var'|'value'), indent
Declares a local variable scoped to the current indent.

7.2 Control flow
v2If condition, target, source, indent
Basic conditional branching.
v2IfAdvanced condition (e.g. ∋, ≒, ≡), target, source, indent
Advanced conditions including approximate match.
v2Else indent
Runs if the preceding v2If condition failed.
v2EndIndent endOfLoop?: boolean, indent
Closes a scope. Jumps back to the loop start if
endOfLoop is true.
v2Loop indent
Infinite loop; runs until v2BreakLoop or script end.
v2LoopNTimes value, valueType, indent
Loops N times (counter kept in temp variables).
v2BreakLoop indent
Exits the current loop.
v2RunTrigger Runs another trigger by name.
v2StopTrigger Immediately ends the current trigger execution.
v2Command Passes a string to the built-in command processor.
[requires low-level access]

Condition operators for v2If / v2IfAdvanced mentioned in the sources:
=, !=, >, < standard comparisons
∈ value is in an array
∋ contains
≡ truthiness
≒ approximate equality
Loop safety: after 100 iterations without a sleep, the system inserts a
1 ms delay to avoid freezing the UI.

7.3 Chat manipulation
v2CutChat start, end, indent Remove messages in a range.
v2ModifyChat index, value, indent Replace text of the message
at the index.
v2SystemPrompt location, value, indent Inject system instructions
into the prompt.
v2Impersonate role, value, indent Force a new message into the
history.
v2QuickSearchChat value, condition, depth, outputVar
Search history for text or a
regex.
v2GetLastMessage, v2GetMessageAtIndex, v2GetMessageCount
Read chat data.

7.4 Data and math
v2SetVar operator (=, +=, *=), var, value
Set or modify a variable.
v2Calculate expression, outputVar
Evaluate a math/logic string.
v2Random min, max, outputVar
Generate a random integer.
v2Tokenize value, outputVar
Token count of a string, using the character's
tokenizer.

7.5 Character / persona data
v2GetCharacterDesc, v2SetCharacterDesc
v2GetPersonaDesc, v2SetPersonaDesc
v2GetAuthorNote, v2SetAuthorNote

7.6 Array
v2MakeArrayVar, v2PushArrayVar, v2PopArrayVar, v2SpliceArrayVar,
v2JoinArrayVar

7.7 Dictionary
v2MakeDictVar, v2SetDictVar, v2GetDictVar, v2DeleteDictKey,
v2GetDictKeys

7.8 String
v2RegexTest, v2ExtractRegex, v2ToLowerCase, v2SplitString,
v2ReplaceString

7.9 Lorebook (full create/read/update/delete access)
Retrieval: v2GetAllLorebooks, v2GetLorebook, v2GetLorebookByName,
v2GetLorebookByIndex
Creation: v2CreateLorebook (name, key, content, insertOrder)
Modification:v2ModifyLorebook,
v2ModifyLorebookByIndex (index, name, key, content,
insertOrder)
Deletion: v2DeleteLorebookByIndex
Activation: v2SetLorebookActivation,
v2SetLorebookAlwaysActive (index, value)

7.10 Display / request state (restricted modes only)
v2GetDisplayState, v2SetDisplayState
v2GetRequestState, v2SetRequestState, v2GetRequestStateRole,
v2SetRequestStateRole, v2GetRequestStateLength

8. LOW-LEVEL ACCESS EFFECTS

───

These require lowLevelAccess on the trigger (and enabling it in the
character settings):
v2RunLLM / runLLM Direct LLM API request. Input is parsed as
ChatML if formatted correctly.
v2SendAIprompt Trigger AI generation.
v2ImgGen / runImgGen Generate an image with the configured provider;
returns an inlay asset reference.
v2ShowAlert,
v2GetAlertInput Show alerts / request user input (normal,
input, or select alerts).
v2Command Run built-in commands.
v2CheckSimilarity Embedding-based similarity between source and
target text (uses embedding models).

9. EXECUTION FLOW

───

• Effects run sequentially in the order defined in the trigger script.
• runTrigger is the main entry point; it also pulls in module triggers.
• V2 indentation controls conditional blocks and loops; scope closes
with v2EndIndent.
• In display and request modes, effects not on the allow list are not
executed.

상태창과 에셋의 기초
refs.note: Basis of how to create an status window, using image assets
refs.text: ### Basic Principles of Creating a Status Window The basic approach is to instruct the AI to output variables for the status window in a specific format at either the beginning or the end of its response. Instructions for this format are usually written in a lorebook and kept permanently active. Example: [Time/Location/Currently Held Items/Inner Thoughts] (If you simply want a particular interface to appear, you can also instruct the AI to output meaningless symbols such as ■□■ that are unlikely to appear naturally during roleplay.) A regex script then reads this format, and display modifications transform it into a well-designed HTML interface. ### How to Use Assets Using character assets follows a similar principle. Depending on factors such as the character's emotions and current state, the AI is instructed to insert a specific format at various points throughout its response. Detailed instructions for this are usually written in a lorebook and kept permanently active. Example: A regex script then reads this format, and display modifications use an expression such as {{raw::$1}} (for example ) to display the character's asset images directly in the chat. Using {{raw::asset name}} is recommended instead of {{img::asset name}}. You can also use HTML to design decorative borders around the assets. #### Duplicate assets If several assets share the same name, the numbered names (asset name.1, asset name.2, ...) must be reflected too, so the instructions must state that numbered variants exist and may be used. Another approach is to use CBS to pick one at random, so the variants appear in varying order. #### Using {{assetlist}} Applying {{assetlist}} lets you pull in every asset at once, without writing each asset name one by one. This is advantageous for a bot where only a single character's assets appear. For a bot with assets of several characters, it can be inefficient, because every character's assets are listed together. In that case it is usually more efficient to write the rule in the form "character name - asset type". Example:

Name: (english name)((korean name))

Facial details: (Hairstyle, hair color, eye shape, eye color, facial features, overall impression, etc.)
Clothing: (The clothing the character typically wears (tops, bottoms, footwear, accessories, equipment, etc.))
